high.title: Stock Investors Hold Their Breath Awaiting Critical Fed Rate Decision
high.summary:
Vietnamese equity and bond markets are on edge ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting concluding July 29. The VN-Index has shed over 200 points from recent peaks, making the market particularly sensitive to any Fed signals. Nguyen The Minh, Head of Investment Banking at An Binh Securities (ABS), notes that U.S. 10-year Treasury yields remain elevated near multi-year highs since 2025, creating persistent external pressure on emerging market assets including VND and Vietnamese government bonds. A growing number of major financial institutions now assign meaningful probability to a Fed rate hike as early as July, driven by rising oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions. **Key implications for VND traders and bond investors:** A hawkish Fed outcome would likely strengthen the USD/VND rate (VND depreciation pressure), widen the spread differential that makes VND assets less attractive, and could trigger foreign capital outflows from Vietnamese equities and bonds. The SBV may need to intervene in FX markets or adjust liquidity management. Watch for VN-Index volatility, government bond yield movements, and any SBV FX intervention signals in the immediate post-Fed window.

---

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on July 28 at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
high.summary:
Vietnam's retail deposit rate landscape continues to show divergence as of July 28, 2026. BaoViet Bank cut rates across multiple tenors — 6-month and 9-month terms trimmed from 6.6% to 6.4% p.a., while 12-month and 18-month tenors were reduced from 6.7% to 6.5% p.a. This move contrasts with ACB, which following a sharp rate hike last week now leads the entire market at 7.8% p.a. for the 12-month tenor, with 6-month and 9-month tenors at 7.6% and 7.7% p.a. respectively. Saigonbank (7.2%) and Bac A Bank (7.1%) rank second and third. Notably, seven banks are now offering rates at or above 7.0% p.a. for 12-month deposits, including MBV, VCBNeo, VIB, and PGBank. The widening dispersion between large state-owned banks and smaller private/joint-stock banks signals continued competition for retail funding. **Key implications:** Elevated deposit rates at smaller banks could pressure net interest margins and indicate liquidity tightening at the margins. The divergence between BaoViet cutting and ACB holding at multi-year highs suggests uneven liquidity conditions across the banking system — a dynamic worth monitoring for bond yield direction and SBV policy response.

---

high.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady But Faces Rare Internal Division — 3 Members Vote Against
high.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 9-3 to hold the federal funds rate unchanged at its latest meeting — marking the first significant internal challenge to new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who assumed the role in May 2026. The three dissenting votes came from regional Fed presidents Beth Hammack (Cleveland), Neel Kashkari (Minneapolis), and Lorie Logan (Dallas), all of whom argued that inflation remains too elevated and that rates should be raised by 25bps immediately. The post-meeting statement confirmed the dissenters "wanted to raise the target federal funds rate by 0.25 percentage points" at this meeting. Prior to the decision, markets largely anticipated a hold, though CME FedWatch data indicated roughly a one-third probability of a surprise hike. The hawkish dissent signals that the Fed's internal policy debate is far from settled, with upside rate risk more live than consensus pricing suggests.

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 29: ACB Leads Market at 7.8% for 12-Month Tenor
high.summary:
Vietnamese bank deposit rates remain meaningfully differentiated across the market as of July 29. ACB continues to lead the 12-month segment at **7.8% p.a.**, also posting the highest rates at medium tenors: 7.6% (6M) and 7.7% (9M). Saigonbank follows at 7.2% and Bac A Bank at 7.1%, with MBV, VCBNeo, VIB, and PGBank all holding at 7.0% — bringing the total number of banks offering ≥7% on 12-month deposits to **seven institutions**.

The four major state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) remain anchored at **6.8% for 12M and 18M tenors**, and 6.6% for 6M/9M, suggesting official reluctance to push benchmark rates higher. MSB holds at 6.8%, Techcombank at 6.75%.

high.title: "Sharks" Quietly Made Their Move Before VN-Index's 200-Point Plunge
high.summary: The VN-Index shed more than 200 points during July 2026, but newly released FiinGroup data reveals that as early as June, a significant number of institutional funds had already begun quietly deploying capital — suggesting informed positioning ahead of the drawdown. In June 2026, 21 out of 37 open-ended equity funds reduced their cash allocations, up from 18/37 in May, indicating that defensive sentiment was already easing even as the broader market remained mixed. The shift was concentrated among larger funds with NAV ranging from VND 1,600–8,800 billion, while smaller funds (sub-VND 1,000 billion) continued to hold elevated cash. VinaCapital funds notably deployed freshly raised capital rather than holding it idle.

medium.title: VN-Index May Still Face a "Shakeout" Phase Before Targeting 1,800 Points — Many Stocks Trading at Rare Valuations with P/E of Only 4–8x
medium.summary:
According to SHS Securities, as of July 22, 2026, the VN-Index stood at 1,668 points with total market capitalization of approximately USD 382 billion, equivalent to 74% of 2025 GDP. Market valuation metrics sit at P/E of 12.09x, P/B of 1.81x, and P/S of 1.44x. Notably, the Vingroup conglomerate alone accounts for roughly USD 91 billion in market cap; excluding this group, the rest of the market trades at a more modest P/E of 10.37x and P/B of 1.53x — levels SHS compares to prior crisis-era market bottoms. The brokerage identifies many fundamentally sound, growth-oriented companies now trading at P/E of only 4–8x with low P/B, presenting potential accumulation opportunities. However, SHS flags a key risk differentiating this cycle from previous bottoms: margin loan-to-market-cap ratios are currently at very elevated levels, suggesting forced selling pressure remains a near-term overhang. The house view is that a further "shakeout" phase is possible before the index can make a sustained move toward 1,800 points. **For fund managers:** the valuation backdrop is becoming supportive for selective equity accumulation, but elevated margin debt warrants caution on timing and position sizing.

---

medium.title: Banks Rush to Issue Certificates of Deposit: Some Double Issuance Volume in Six Months
medium.summary:
Vietnamese commercial banks have significantly ramped up issuance of Certificates of Deposit (CDs) in H1 2026, signaling intensifying competition for medium-to-long-term funding to support accelerating credit growth. ACB stands out with outstanding CD balances reaching VND 160,355 billion at end-June 2026 — a near doubling (+98%) compared to end-2025. Notably, 1-2 year tenor CDs surged 6.5x, indicating banks are actively locking in longer-duration liabilities. This aggressive CD issuance reflects tightening liquidity conditions in the banking system and is broadly indicative of upward pressure on deposit rates and wholesale funding costs. For bond market participants, rising bank funding costs could spill over into higher lending rates and potentially compress net interest margins, while also competing with government bonds for investor appetite. This trend warrants monitoring for its pass-through effect on market interest rates and the broader rate environment.

---

medium.title: 54 Funds Collectively Accumulate a Bank Stock — What Is Happening?
medium.summary:
According to FiinGroup's latest report, Vietnamese open-ended equity funds shifted back into deployment mode in June 2026 after increasing cash buffers in May. 21 out of 37 funds reduced their cash allocation in June, up from 18/37 in May, suggesting that defensive positioning is gradually unwinding — even as the VN-Index edged lower and market breadth remained mixed. Most funds with NAV between VND 1,600–8,800 billion reduced cash holdings. VinaCapital funds notably maintained net inflows, with newly raised capital being deployed rather than held as cash. Smaller funds (NAV below VND 1,000 billion) were the primary exception, continuing to accumulate cash. On the stock selection side, the banking sector dominated fund flows: ACB, OCB, BID (BIDV), and VCB (Vietcombank) all saw net buying. ACB stood out most sharply, with 54 funds participating in net purchases — the largest coordinated accumulation observed. The closed-end fund VEIL was the largest single buyer. **Implication for equity investors:** The rotation back into banking stocks by institutional funds signals cautious optimism on Vietnamese financials, and is worth monitoring as a leading indicator of broader VN-Index sentiment and potential upside in major bank counters.

---

medium.title: Banks Reporting Profit Declines in H1 2026 — Saigonbank, Eximbank, Sacombank, LPBank Among the Laggards
medium.summary: Of 17 banks that have disclosed H1 2026 results so far, the majority reported year-on-year profit growth, but four banks — Saigonbank (SGB), Eximbank (EIB), Sacombank, and LPBank — posted earnings declines. Saigonbank recorded the steepest fall, with pre-tax profit of only VND 48 billion in H1, down 72% YoY; the bank posted a pre-tax loss of VND 40 billion in Q2 alone, making it the first Vietnamese bank to report a quarterly loss in Q2 2026. The deterioration was driven by broad-based income weakness across business lines combined with a 62.4% surge in provisioning costs to over VND 64 billion. Eximbank's pre-tax profit came in at an estimated VND 730 billion (full figures pending). While these are smaller, non-systemic institutions, the provisioning pressure signals rising asset quality stress in pockets of the banking sector, which is relevant for assessing credit risk spreads and the outlook for lending rate normalization under SBV's guidance.

medium.title: Trump Comments Trigger 7% Oil Price Spike — Iran Tensions Escalate
medium.summary:
Brent crude surged 7.4% to $90.35/barrel and WTI jumped 7.4% to $85.11/barrel following a sharp escalation in US-Iran tensions. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched ballistic missiles targeting US forces at a base in Jordan, which were intercepted by CENTCOM. President Trump warned Iran "will be defeated" and pledged a strong military response. US and Saudi forces subsequently struck multiple logistics sites in eastern Iraq in retaliation for over 30 drone attacks in three days. This geopolitical shock has direct implications for Vietnam: as a net energy importer, a sustained oil price spike above $90/barrel will pressure Vietnam's trade balance and import costs, adding to inflationary risks. This complicates the SBV's already delicate balancing act between supporting growth and defending the VND. Elevated oil prices could widen Vietnam's current account deficit, increasing downward pressure on VND/USD. Watch for any SBV response or FX intervention signals in the coming sessions.

---
